cell_type: # Bat (Eonycteris spelaea) Whole Blood scRNA-seq Cell Markers
# Basis: orthologous translation from human unless stated
# All gene names follow human HGNC nomenclature (applied via
# TIER 1 — T CELLS (pan-T marker genes shared across all T subtypes)

basis: TCR complex subunit; deeply conserved across all jawed vertebrates; validated in multiple bat species (Pteropus alecto; Rhinolophus spp.)
TCR complex subunit; co-expressed with CD3D; same conservation basis
MHC class II co-receptor; protein sequence >85% identity to human; used in bat flow cytometry cross-reactivity studies (Clayton et al. 2023 PLoS Pathog)
IL-7 receptor; conserved but expressed on both CD4 and CD8 memory T cells — not CD4-specific; broadens CD4 T score
Lymph node homing receptor; conserved but also marks naive CD8 T cells; bat-specific expression breadth unclear
TCR complex; see CD4 T above
TCR complex; see CD4 T above
MHC class I co-receptor alpha chain; 12.1% cells +ve in bat dataset; highly conserved; validated cross-species (Subudhi et al. 2022 Nat Commun)
MHC class I co-receptor beta chain; 10.5% cells +ve; co-expressed with CD8A; same conservation basis
Granzyme K; 21% cells +ve — too broad; also in CD4 T (effector) and NK; granzyme family diverged in chiroptera; should be removed
TCR complex; see above
TCR complex; see above
Master Treg transcription factor; extremely conserved across mammals; bat FOXP3 orthologue confirmed in Pteropus and Eonycteris genomes
CD25; IL-2 receptor alpha; conserved; co-expressed with FOXP3 in regulatory T cells
Immune checkpoint receptor; extremely conserved; used in bat immune studies as Treg marker proxy

cell_type: # TIER 1 — T CELL SUBTYPES (used after top-level CD4 T assignment)

basis: Lymph node homing; conserved but shared with memory CD8 T; moderate specificity
CD62L; 50.4% cells +ve in bat blood — not discriminating; bat selectin biology may differ from human; recommend removal
TCF-1; Wnt pathway TF essential for naive T identity; deeply conserved; validated in bat T cells (Subudhi et al. 2022)
Wnt pathway TF; co-expressed with TCF7 in naive T cells; deeply conserved
Granzyme K; see CD8 T note above — shared with NK and CD8 T; should be replaced
Granzyme B; cytotoxic; conserved but also in NK and CD8 T effectors; moderate specificity for CD4 effectors
OX40 co-stimulatory receptor; marks activated/effector CD4 T cells; conserved across mammals
Perforin; cytotoxic marker; conserved but shared with NK and CD8 T effectors
Shared with naive T and CD8 memory — not memory-specific; conserved but lacks specificity
Aquaporin 3; used as human memory CD4 T marker (Gattinoni et al.); no bat-specific validation; may reflect general membrane biology
EBI2 chemokine receptor; conserved; expressed on memory B and T cells; moderate specificity
Alarmin/metastasin; broadly expressed across many cell types including monocytes and fibroblasts; poor T cell specificity

cell_type: # TIER 1 — γδ T CELLS (bat-specific addition; genes present in merged GTF since Dec 2024)

basis: TCR delta constant region; defines γδ T lineage; conserved across mammals; added to bat GTF Dec 2024
TCR gamma constant 1; conserved; used in bat γδ T identification (Papenfuss et al.)
TCR gamma constant 2; conserved; co-expressed with TRGC1
Granule membrane protein 7; among the most conserved NK/cytotoxic markers across mammals; high expression (28.9% bat cells)
Granulysin; antimicrobial peptide; present in bat GTF but granulysin genes show copy number variation across bat families (Chiroptera); moderate confidence
CD94; NKG2 heterodimer partner; NK receptor superfamily diversified in bats — Chiroptera have expanded KLRB/KLRC families; orthologous function assumed
CD20; MS4A gene family has expanded in some bat lineages (Jebb et al. 2020 Nature); core B cell marker but bat-specific expression fidelity less certain than CD19/CD79A
Igα; BCR signalling complex; extremely conserved across all B cell-bearing vertebrates; validated in bat B cells
BCR co-receptor; highly conserved; validated in bat B cell identification studies

cell_type: # BAT OVERRIDE — B cell subtypes (isotype genes IGHD/IGHM/IGHG1 absent from bat GTF annotation)

basis: Proto-oncogene; expressed in naive/transitional B cells; conserved but limited bat-specific validation
IL-4 receptor; conserved; expressed on naive B and T cells; moderate specificity
Heat-stable antigen; conserved; expressed on transitional/naive B cells; also on some T cells and DC
CD23; low-affinity IgE receptor; IgE biology present in bats; conserved but FCER2 expression in naive B cells has limited bat-specific validation
TNF receptor superfamily member 7; canonical memory B cell marker; highly conserved; used as human-ortholog memory B marker in bat studies
TACI; conserved transmembrane receptor for BAFF/APRIL; expressed on memory B and plasma cells; moderate specificity
Inflammasome sensor; expressed on memory B cells in humans (Weill et al.); no bat-specific validation for this context; used as surrogate

cell_type: # TIER 3 — PLASMA CELLS (top-level scType and B cell subtype)

basis: Marginal zone B and B1 cell-specific protein; conserved; only 0.2% bat cells +ve — very low expression; requires co-scoring with other markers
Immunoglobulin J chain; links IgM/IgA polymers; among most conserved immunoglobulin-related genes; 1.8% bat cells +ve
CD138/syndecan-1; canonical plasma cell surface marker; highly conserved; 3.8% bat cells +ve
Ectoenzyme; highly and broadly expressed on plasma cells; conserved across mammals; 0.7% bat cells +ve (low but concentrated on plasma clusters)
ER stress transcription factor; master regulator of antibody-secreting cell differentiation; deeply conserved; 12.1% bat cells +ve
BLIMP-1; master transcription factor for plasma cell differentiation; extremely conserved across all vertebrates; 6.4% bat cells +ve
LPS co-receptor; innate immunity; ancient and highly conserved across all mammals; validated in bat monocytes by flow cytometry
Lysozyme; antimicrobial enzyme; one of the most ancient and conserved innate immunity genes; high expression expected in monocytes across species
Cystatin C; cysteine protease inhibitor; conserved; expressed in monocytes and DC; validated cross-species
Calgranulin A; alarmin; S100 family broadly conserved but bat-specific expression distribution not validated; also expressed in neutrophils
Calgranulin B; co-expressed with S100A8 (MRP8/14 complex); same conservation basis

cell_type: # BAT OVERRIDE — FCGR3A absent from bat annotation; FCGR2A substituted

basis: CD32A; FcγRIIa; Fc receptor family has duplications/divergence in bats; FCGR3A absent from ESpe GTF so FCGR2A used as substitute — conserved function but not orthologous marker
CD16B; neutrophil-associated in human but used here for non-classical mono scoring in bat; FCGR family divergent — moderate confidence
p57/KIP2; cell cycle inhibitor; marks patrolling/non-classical monocytes; highly conserved across mammals
MS4A family member; non-classical monocyte marker in human; MS4A family variable in bats (Jebb et al. 2020); moderate confidence

cell_type: # BAT OVERRIDE — CEACAM8 dropped (highly divergent in bats); IDO1 and CEACAM6 added

basis: CD16B; neutrophil-specific Fc receptor in human; FCGR gene family has diverged in bats — not independently validated in bat neutrophils
G-CSF receptor; master granulopoiesis receptor; extremely conserved across all mammals; defines neutrophil/granulocyte lineage
IL-8 receptor; neutrophil chemoattractant receptor; conserved; validated as neutrophil marker across mammalian species
CEACAM family member; bat CEACAM family is divergent (faster-evolving genes); CEACAM8 dropped from bat annotation; CEACAM6 retained as partial substitute — moderate confidence
Indoleamine 2
column6: 3-dioxygenase 1; bat-specific addition; IDO1 upregulated in bat innate immune cells (Banerjee et al. 2020 iScience) — bat-informed marker

cell_type: # NOTE: Eosinophil and Mast cell treated as contamination/rare in bat whole blood

basis: SIGLEC family rapidly evolving in mammals; bat SIGLEC8 ortholog unconfirmed; human marker only
Eotaxin receptor; conserved; expressed on eosinophils/basophils; moderate specificity
Eosinophil peroxidase; conserved enzymatic marker; present in bat GTF
Tryptase alpha/beta 1; mast cell-specific serine protease; highly conserved across mammals
Carboxypeptidase A3; mast cell-specific; conserved; validated cross-species
FcεRI beta chain; IgE receptor subunit; conserved in bats (IgE present); moderate confidence for bat mast cells
c-Kit/CD117; stem cell factor receptor; conserved; marks mast cells and HSPCs

cell_type: # Basophil — detected by SingleR (MonacoImmune) only; no scType marker set defined

basis: Basophil detection relies entirely on MonacoImmune reference; no explicit marker genes in scType scoring; cross-species reference validity unconfirmed for bat
High-affinity IgE receptor alpha; IgE biology conserved in bats; expressed on plasmacytoid DC and mast cells; not exclusively cDC in bat — moderate confidence
DNGR-1; dead cell sensor; marks cDC1 lineage; highly conserved in all mammals; validated in multiple non-human species
CXCL7/beta-thromboglobulin; platelet-specific chemokine; extremely conserved; highest confidence platelet marker
CXCL4/platelet factor 4; conserved across all mammals; definitive platelet marker
Haemoglobin beta; extremely conserved; definitive RBC marker
Haemoglobin alpha 1; extremely conserved; definitive RBC marker
Haemoglobin alpha 2; conserved; RBC-specific
Glycophorin A; red cell surface sialoglycoprotein; bat RBCs are nucleated (unlike human) — GYPA expression may differ; moderate confidence
Sialomucin; hematopoietic progenitor marker; conserved across all vertebrates
Transcription factor; essential for HSC development; extremely conserved; expressed in early haematopoietic progenitors and megakaryocytes
Arginine vasopressin; primarily a neurohypophyseal hormone; included as megakaryocyte/HSPC marker in some datasets; unusual choice — limited PBMC validation; low confidence
